Figure 1:Sequence-prior performance depends on the representation extraction.A: masked loss on 512 windows. NTv3 uses fixed 12% additional masking
(†\dagger), averaging losses over two draws.
GENERATORv2 uses temperature calibration fitted on separate data (‡\ddagger).

Figure 5:Selecting edits for a desired
response and cell specificity.A/B: rank of the first selected edit and success at matching a
reference-edit response as testing budget increases
(331 targets, 110 regulatory elements).
C: target-cell expression increase versus absolute other-cell
change across 127 loci, varying the penalty on unwanted effects.
Open markers ignore the other cell (λ=0\lambda=0), and filled markers penalize it equally (λ=1\lambda=1). Experimental references in A–C select edits on one group of repeat
measurements and evaluate on the other. Models may outperform these references.
D: task settings.†\daggermarks native outputs in A, and whiskers show 95% element-bootstrap intervals.

Figure 6:Selecting DNA with activity
in desired cells and little activity elsewhere.Models choose ten enhancers for each of sixteen requested expression patterns.
A: gain in utility over random selection among sequences originally
designed for the same ON/OFF pattern, averaged across patterns.
Utility rewards the weakest ON-cell activity and penalizes the
strongest OFF-cell activity above the negative-control level.
Dots show the two repeat measurements.
The experimental reference selects sequences using one measurement
and evaluates them using the other, then swaps them.
B: example across cell types, showing ten enhancers chosen by AlphaGenome having selective activity in HepG2 and K562.
